newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison shares fall amid bid speculation.
newsitem.headline: Morrison shares fall amid bid speculation.

text.p: Shares of Morrison Petroleums Ltd fell in busy volume on Wednesday, driving market watchers to speculate that a new development in its takeover battle with suitor Canadian 88 Energy Corp was about to unfold.
Morrison, target of Canadian 88's hostile C$652 million bid, was down 0.30 to 10 in Toronto Stock Exchange trade with nearly 1.5 million shares changing hands.

Canadian 88, embattled recently over an investigation into trading in Morrison stock by a private firm before the bid was launched, was up 0.20 to 5.95, bringing the share-swap value of its bid to 8.93.
Canadian 88 has offered C$10 cash, to a maximum cash portion of C$140 million, or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.

One Calgary-based investment industry source close to the deal, when asked if he believed that the takeover situation was expected to change in the near future, said: "I think you're getting the right signals."

Paul Charron, Morrison's vice-president of finance, would offer no details regarding the state of the deal late Tuesday or early on Wednesday, but said his firm was urging shareholders to "stop, look and listen" and not tender to the Canadian 88 offer.
It was unknown whether that meant a white knight for Morrison was in the wings or if Canadian 88 was poised to pull its offer off the table, said several sources.
Canadian 88 chief executive Greg Noval was not immediately available for comment on Wednesday.
A list of companies that had been rumored as potential rival bidders included Talisman Energy Inc, Norcen Energy Resources Ltd, Rigel Energy Corp.
Another source close to the deal said Morrison's data room continued to be the site of brisk traffic and said that a white knight might not come forward "until the 11th hour."
